To anyone who feels soulslike's are not your cup of tea, haven't tried any and do not intend to - this game could be the perfect gateway to the genre; without the jank and a lenient, more conservative learning curve. I went into this expecting a brutal challenge and came out pleasantly surprised at how balanced and enjoyable ALL of the boss fights were. There was no fight that took me more than an hour to beat and when I did, the satisfaction was immense.

Game is absolutely gorgeous, the various tools at your disposal make the Sun Wukong power fantasy extremely satisfying and the visuals, boss designs are on point. My only issues with the game were its exploration, which often was unintuitive and made things VERY easy to miss. Also to anyone unfamiliar with the whole Journey to the West storyline, some lore aspects will require further reading and looking up. Overall, 10/10 and should have won GOTY no questions asked.

Great game if you enjoy souls likes. It has probably the biggest variety of bosses of any game and each boss is different with unique moves. The movement and combat is also much more refined compared to other souls likes (except maybe Sekiro), the animations are great and attacks flow really nicely. During the combat, the bosses might sometimes interrupt you mid attack, like catch your staff mid hit and perform a mini scripted move on you, which might sound lame, but is executed so well in this case, making the combat feel more alive and spectacular. The level design is semi open-world, which makes it quiet linear, but I think it plays well into the story telling. The story is also simple but intriguing, you don't need to watch 10hrs of youtube videos to understand whats going on (like in Elden Ring) or to simply progress through the game. The biggest weakness is the general performance and upscaling implementation, dlss, fsr both look quite bad especially in the dark areas and you have to use it if you want to play at acceptable frame rate.

Well, I don't l know nothing about anything, but I liked the game. I liked the story, visuals, music, voice-acting, and most of all the fact that you can cheese (in a broad sense - there is always an item, armor or whatnot) most of the bosses. Matter of fact, I liked the game so much, midway through it I read the "Monkey King" (this is an abridged 300 pages long version of the original myth). This gave a lot of context to the characters. But you don't have to read the book to be excited about the story - copious, beautifully illustrated pages of lore are there, along with cinematics, to keep you in the mythical world of Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, and coincidentally Buddha Victorious in Struggle, formerly known as the Great Sage Equal to Heaven. It is fucking epic, immersive, beautiful, and it's an unapologetic boss-rush. There is a boss like every twenty goddam minutes, 45 bosses in total are required and a bunch are optional. Good thing the game is forgiving with dodge timings, combat is smooth, and you have a vast arsenal of spells and other cool stuff. I really enjoyed it, but my thumb is sore from pressing B on a controller. I reckon, it's a small price to pay (in many ways btw).

Review After 100% Achievements

Really enjoyed my journey through this title! Combat feels really great with the stance swapping mechanics. If you like boss fights, this is the game for you, with there being like 90+ for you to conquer. Some more challenging than others, but all are unique and memorable for you to tackle again on your next playthrough in NG+. Everything in this game works well together; the spirts, spells, vessels…all of them made for some really cool variety in gameplay. The ability to change your build on the fly is a huge plus and I loved the chapter-to-chapter format of the story. Animated cutscene story tales were an awesome touch to bring each chapter to a close. Most of all, I loved finding all the hidden areas and questlines along the way, figuring out secret items and bosses that you might not run into without exploring. All of the achievements were fun to go after, collecting all items and defeating every enemy to complete your journal is an awesome feeling to accomplish. This game deserves all the positive feedback it’s receiving and I hope to see DLC/a sequel in the future!

I’ve really been enjoying Black Myth: Wukong. The graphics are absolutely marvelous, and the overall story is really good and keeps you hooked. The bosses are definitely hard, but honestly, that is what makes the game so fun because you actually have to take the time to learn their attack patterns to win. The combat mechanics are amazing, with my personal favorites being the Smash and Thrust stances. There is nothing quite as satisfying as calling in my clones and just bumping enemies into oblivion using the Smash stance. Another huge plus for me is the sheer amount of main and side quests. It keeps the game from being too easy or quick to end, which is exactly what I want since I don't really like fast paced games that are over in a flash. Overall, it is just a fantastic, rewarding experience.

One very important thing about this game that I think you don't see when you watch videos on it is that the combat is very scripted and doesn't flow like other souls-like games. In other games of this genre, the combat has a very distinct flow that I personally just didn't get with this game. It felt like the only thing going for it in terms of combat was flashiness. Another thing I didn't enjoy was the movement. God, the movement in this game felt so restrictive, which is very prominent in most souls-like games, but the marketing for this game made it seem more like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice when in reality you have much less freedom. One thing this game does have going for it is it's graphics. God this game is beautiful. While the combat isn't too good, the look of this game is amazing. The opening fight in this game felt so climactic and made me think this game was something special. Overall, if you've read this and seen all the trailers and still felt like this game is right for you, go buy it. It's obviously had so much work put into it by so many talented people, but I just felt like there were some things they weren't telling you
This is a well-written continuation of *Journey to the West*. We are witnessing the rise of Eastern games.

If I were to rate this game, I would give it a 9. The graphics deserve a 10, but there is still a bit of room for improvement in terms of game balance. As a bilingual speaker fluent in both Chinese and English, I have been familiar with the story of "Journey to the West" since childhood, and this game has fulfilled a childhood dream of mine. I hope that more top-tier game IPs like this one will emerge. Many countries around the world have rich mythologies, from Sparta to Egypt, from Japan's Amaterasu to Greek myths, or even the myths of the Sumerian civilization, as well as other Chinese mythological stories like "The Classic of Mountains and Seas." I hope that one day, these can all be transformed into top-tier games, allowing me to experience them through VR.

This game’s graphics are absolutely breathtaking, and the amount of historical reference woven into every detail is incredible. It flawlessly blends the spirit of Chinese mythology and cultivation manhwa with deep storytelling and cinematic presentation.

The combat mechanics feel smooth, weighty, and deeply satisfying — you can tell how much dedication and artistry went into crafting each chapter. The historical and cultural depth is truly mind-blowing and makes every encounter feel meaningful.

I highly recommend playing it in Chinese audio with English subtitles — it captures the soul of the story perfectly.

The only downside is the navigation and map system, which can be a bit confusing at times. But aside from that, this is a fantastic experience — easily one of the best action RPGs I’ve ever played.

Sure you have some of the occasional annoying bosses you need a bit more than a handful to beat, but then you have bosses with horrible hitboxes and mechanics that, at least for me, made it too impossible to have fun in. But overall the game is pretty decent.

It can be fun sometimes and it has a good story, and, even though i don't really care about graphics, they looked good. The problem is that the combat is so boring after just a few hours and it's just dodging and hitting with the trump card of using spells that take too long to regenerate during a boss fight after first use. Also, there are so many bosses in close proximity that almost none of them are memorable.

Black Myth: Wukong is one of my favourite games of all time. Unlike souls-like titles most of the non-boss enemies are relatively easy giving the player more freedom in their exploration. Skill points can be reset at anytime allowing for build changes without much thought. The bosses are hard but fair to keep you trying again until victory, every attempt learning a new way to dodge or a new move to attack with. The graphics are stunning, the bosses are incredible and its' ties to chinese folklore give it a charm that no other game i have played has. 

I honestly believe this game is a masterpiece and was robbed of GOTY 2024
